stories.Headline: India's Manufacturing Future Will Be Built by Engineers Who Understand How the World's Best Products Are Made
stories.Summary:
Caresoft Global and DRIIV, an organization under India's Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser, have partnered to improve engineering talent development across the country. The collaboration aims to expose Indian engineering students to global manufacturing practices and contemporary industrial knowledge, addressing a gap where graduates typically have strong theoretical training but limited exposure to how world-class products are designed and manufactured. Adroit Technologies Innovative Solutions joins as the implementation partner.

The initiative will establish Centers of Excellence throughout India and develop specialized programs focused on emerging technology sectors including electric vehicles, software-defined vehicles, high-voltage battery systems, semiconductors, and artificial intelligence. Using Caresoft Global's Iceberg platform, which provides engineering benchmarking and technology intelligence, the program will help students and professionals understand how leading manufacturers make decisions about design, performance, quality, and cost. The partnership addresses India's need for engineers equipped with contemporary skills as the nation advances toward higher-value manufacturing and globally integrated supply chains.

stories.Headline: US to Tell Countries to Pick a Side in The AI Race. Choosing China Could Cost Them Access to The Washington Coalition.
stories.Summary:
The United States is preparing to pressure 35 countries that signed its AI Opportunity Statement to choose between supporting American or Chinese artificial intelligence initiatives. According to internal documents reviewed by Reuters, the State Department plans to send a letter warning these nations that they cannot simultaneously participate in both the U.S.-led Pax Silica coalition and China's competing World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. The message emphasizes that countries must make a deliberate choice, stating that membership in one framework cannot coexist with participation in conflicting initiatives.

Pax Silica, launched last year, aims to secure supply chains for advanced AI technology including semiconductors and critical minerals, with roughly two dozen countries already participating, such as Japan, Australia, and South Korea. Kazakhstan has emerged as a test case, having joined both the U.S. and Chinese frameworks, making it the only known country in both blocs. Chinese officials oppose the forced choice, arguing it will harm global AI progress, while U.S. officials insist countries cannot credibly maintain relationships with both competing ecosystems.

stories.Headline: The Millennium Group of Schools Launches 'Millennium AI Creators Championship 2026' to Inspire India's Next Generation of Responsible AI Creators
stories.Summary:
The Millennium Group of Schools announced the launch of the Millennium AI Creators Championship 2026, a national competition designed to encourage students in grades 5 through 12 across India to use artificial intelligence responsibly while developing creativity and innovation skills. The championship is free to enter, with registration opening on August 15 and closing on August 31, 2026. The competition features three age-specific categories including storytelling for grades 5-7, song creation for grades 8-9, and short film creation for grades 10-12, all centered around the theme "Sustainable Cities. Intelligent Futures."

The initiative aims to engage over 25,000 students, 50,000 parents and 2,000 educators through partnerships with Times Now as the official broadcast partner. Winners will be announced on September 12, and the top 15 national winners will receive a fully sponsored AI Fellowship with advanced learning opportunities and robotics kits. Participants will also receive complimentary access to expert-led sessions on prompt engineering, artificial intelligence ethics and digital citizenship to help them develop responsible AI skills.

stories.Headline: NIELIT Launches CYBER KUSHTI 2026: National Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon scores judgment rather than detection speed
stories.Summary:
NIELIT, the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology, launched CYBER KUSHTI 2026 on August 15th as a national cybersecurity and artificial intelligence hackathon. The competition differs from traditional cybersecurity contests by focusing on human judgment rather than speed of detection. Free registration opened on August 15th and closes September 10th, with teams of three students and independent researchers eligible to participate. Each team receives an identical package containing deliberately flawed security assessments with false findings, duplicates, and omissions to evaluate and prioritize.

The hackathon unfolds in three rounds, starting with an online round on September 15th selecting 50 teams, followed by another online round on September 24th narrowing to 10 finalists. The final round occurs in person on October 9th in New Delhi at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre. Judges from government, industry, and academia will evaluate participants' ability to identify genuine issues and correctly reject false findings. The winning team receives the title "Cyber Kesari 2026," while runners-up receive "Rustam" and "Pahalwan" titles.

stories.Headline: Onemeta OTCQB (ONEI): August 17th 2026; Reports Over 500% Increase in Verbum Call Consumption amid new client intake, including Fortune 500 Companies, Producing $2.4M Positive Cash Flow During H1 2026
stories.Summary:
Onemeta Inc., an AI-powered multilingual communication company, reported significant growth in its VerbumCall platform during the first half of 2026. The company saw consumption increase over 500% from January through June, onboarded more than 20 new enterprise clients including several Fortune 500 companies, and generated $2.4 million in positive operating cash flow during the first six months of the year. The company also signed a three-year reseller agreement with Avaya worth $3 million in prepaid service credits and repurchased shares to strengthen its capital structure.

Management attributes the momentum to disciplined execution of its go-to-market strategy, which focuses on partnerships with contact center service providers to embed AI-powered translation directly into enterprise systems. The company expanded its compliance credentials by achieving ISO 27001 certification and broadened access to government procurement channels. While reported revenue declined from the prior year due to timing of licensing fees, leadership views the rapid client installation and platform consumption growth as stronger indicators of underlying business momentum and expects this adoption to convert into recurring revenue.

stories.Headline: 'Nation First-Rashtra Pratham' should remain the guiding principle: VP Radhakrishnan at SRMIST convocation
stories.Summary:
Vice President CP Radhakrishnan addressed the 22nd convocation at SRM Institute of Science and Technology in Chennai, urging graduating students to adopt "Nation First - Rashtra Pratham" as their guiding principle. He emphasized that graduates should use their knowledge, skills and innovation for nation-building and preparing themselves to shape the future. Radhakrishnan praised the institution's focus on emerging fields including artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, semiconductor research and sustainable development, noting that research achieves its highest purpose when it serves society and produces practical benefits for people.

The Vice President highlighted India's educational expansion since 2014, with the establishment of numerous universities and institutes across the country. He noted that female enrollment in higher education increased by 42.2 percent from 2014-15 to 2023-24, rising from 1.57 crore to 2.24 crore students. Radhakrishnan also urged graduates to avoid drugs and substance abuse, referencing a recent tragic incident in Tamil Nadu. He encouraged students to uphold constitutional values, respect diversity and place national interest above personal gain, while embodying the Indian values of knowledge, duty, compassion and service.

stories.Headline: Over 4,000 abandoned mine pits in Plateau – Alake
stories.Summary:
The Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, reported that over 4,000 abandoned mine pits are scattered across Plateau State. These pits, largely created by former mining companies, present serious environmental and safety hazards. The announcement came after seven people died in a collapsed mine pit in Kassa, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area. Alake emphasized that the tragedy was preventable and warned unauthorized artisanal miners against entering abandoned pits without proper licenses and permits.

The federal government has already rehabilitated 59 of these abandoned pits and plans to rehabilitate more. Alake stated that the ministry is using Geographic Information System satellite mapping and artificial intelligence technology to identify and assess the remaining pits, with Plateau serving as the initial pilot location. The minister encouraged private investors to partner with the government to convert these abandoned sites into productive ventures such as energy, tourism, and fisheries projects. He also called on miners to organize into cooperatives and obtain necessary legal approvals to operate properly.

stories.Headline: Netanyahu's Likud Party holds primaries ahead of Israel's general elections | Benjamin Netanyahu News
stories.Summary:
Israel's governing Likud Party held primaries to select candidates for an upcoming general election that is seen as particularly significant for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the party. The right-wing Likud Party has dominated Israeli politics since 1977, shifting the country's political center rightward and supporting military operations including the ongoing conflict in Gaza. Under Israel's proportional representation system, parties submit ranked candidate lists, and the Likud's top positions are largely predetermined through party leadership and coalition deals.

Netanyahu personally controls eleven of the top thirty realistic candidacies, with additional spots reserved for Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and Defence Minister Israel Katz through prior agreements. Both ministers have taken hardline positions on Gaza, with Katz calling for cutting utilities and humanitarian aid to the territory, while Saar supported ethnic cleansing efforts. Netanyahu also nominated tech entrepreneur Oren Dobronsky, who recently apologized for insulting comments about President Trump and had previously stated that Gaza should be leveled with no Palestinians remaining.

stories.Headline: Peoples Reflections Marks Seven Years of Empowering Journalism, Launches Reflections Gurukul to Prepare Journalists for the AI Era
stories.Summary:
Peoples Reflections, an organization that has spent seven years recognizing journalistic excellence across 48+ countries, has launched Reflections Gurukul, a new educational platform designed to prepare journalists for the artificial intelligence era. The initiative addresses a significant gap in journalism education, as AI technology rapidly transforms the profession through applications in research, content creation, fact-checking, and newsroom operations, yet many aspiring journalists lack structured training in using these tools responsibly while maintaining journalistic integrity.

Reflections Gurukul combines AI journalism education, practical learning opportunities, internships, publishing platforms, and royalty-based earning options for qualified writers. Rather than offering only certificates, the platform enables learners to build professional portfolios through actual journalism work and aims to develop journalists who can combine technical AI literacy with critical thinking, human creativity, and journalistic ethics. The initiative leverages Peoples Reflections' international network to provide global exposure and cross-cultural understanding as the platform expands.

stories.Headline: Washington should stop creating division
stories.Summary:
The United States is preparing to pressure 35 countries that signed an artificial intelligence agreement to choose between working with America or China. According to a draft letter from the State Department, nations will face exclusion from a US-led AI coalition if they also participate in China's competing framework. The US aims to create a technology bloc that would restrict China's access to essential resources for developing advanced AI systems.

This exclusionary approach risks fragmenting global supply chains and damaging international cooperation in artificial intelligence development. Critics argue that forcing countries to pick sides weaponizes technological competition and undermines the innovation ecosystem that benefits from open collaboration. China's embassy rejected the strategy as harmful to global AI progress. The article contends that nations need inclusive governance and multilateral cooperation to address AI challenges, rather than divisive barriers that ultimately weaken all participants.
